title: Summable nonnegative families have summable finite-subset products
statement: Let $I$ be any set and let $u:I\to\mathbf R$ satisfy $u_i\geq0$ for every $i\in I$. Suppose that $u$ is summable, where summability of an indexed real family means convergence of the net of its sums over finite subsets of its index set in the usual absolute-value metric of [def-weil-complex-absolute-value] restricted to the real numbers. Then the family indexed by the set $\operatorname{Finset}(I)$ of all finite subsets of $I$, given by $S\mapsto\prod_{i\in S}u_i$, is summable. The product for $S=\varnothing$ is $1$.
